title: lampOS: let the eyes say how much each face's mouth moves, behind LAMP_EYES_MOUTH (task 39, #720)
body:
Part of #720

**Kind:** off unless set.

**The study** (`docs/eyes.md`, "Whether a mouth moves", with sources): frame differences round the lips, optical flow, MediaPipe's lip landmarks, Light-ASD, TalkNet, and what Furhat, Misty, Jibo and Astro publish (nothing found). Taken first: frame differences of the lower face less those of the eyes, from YuNet's own marks, because it costs under a millisecond a frame on the CPU and works on a 25-pixel mouth; a landmark model needs a larger face than 320 by 240 gives at a metre, and Light-ASD needs the sound, which on this lamp carries the lamp's own voice. Next rung if the recordings say it cannot part speech from chewing: Light-ASD's visual half on the NPU.

**The switch:** `LAMP_EYES_MOUTH=on` beside `LAMP_BUS=on`. The eyes then read every frame while a face is in view (not only the four a second the detector looks at) and say on `humans/faces/mouths`, under each face's id from `humans/faces/tracked`, how much its mouth moves from 0 to 1 over 0.5 s, how many frames that was, and how old the newest frame is. Without it no frame is read for mouths, the topic is not declared, and `humans/faces/tracked` is byte for byte as before: `mouths_are_said_only_when_asked_and_the_faces_are_said_alike_either_way`. Synthetic frames: `a_moving_mouth_scores_high_a_still_face_low_and_a_turning_head_not_as_speech` and two more in `mouth.rs`.

**Board cost, lamp-52e6** (`docs/verification/mouth-moving-lamp-52e6-20261014/`): 0.6 to 1.1 ms a frame against 61 to 89 ms a look for the detector, nothing with nobody in view; 116 to 135 ms from a frame's taking to its read; 22 MB, 15% of one core; 51 to 52 °C. A talking face on the Mac's display was found too seldom (16 to 18% of the picture, 20 of 178 looks) to judge the score.

**Gate:** `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p lamp-eyes --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean on macOS and in `rust:1.96.0-bookworm` ARM64; `cargo test -p lamp-eyes` 26 + 2 passed, 0 failed; `cargo build --workspace` ok. Native ARM64 run on dc7b28997 green: https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/actions/runs/38584641985 (CI 38584641564 green).

**Left for a person (why this is a draft):** the recordings: talking to the lamp, over it while it speaks, silent and facing it, chewing and smiling, two people. `mouths.sh` in the verification folder runs them in about ten minutes and writes numbers only; the build is installed on lamp-52e6, not run. `FULL` (six grey levels) and the window are set from them.

title: lampOS: tell the model what follows an early end is the rest of the request cut off, and probe that note
body:
Closes #723

Step 2 of `second-P1`, on what lamp-4ace showed at 23:10: (a) does not hold, (b) does.

**Kind: off unless set.** Everything changed in the voice happens only with `--early-end-ms`, which no unit sets since 13:46. The successor of a request whose end was sent early and given up (`continue_after_early_end`) is started with `continues_cut_off`, and the provider worker writes a note beside that request. No other request is ever marked.

**The switch, and the test that nothing changes without it.** The switch is `--early-end-ms`:
- `a_start_is_written_as_before_unless_it_goes_on_from_one_cut_off`: a start without the flag serializes byte for byte as before (the flag is left off the wire when false), and an old start reads as not cut off.
- The early-end session test of a request quiet to the end compares its whole wire and finds no note.
- Every other voice test passes unchanged, except the two early-end tests that now expect the note.

**What it is** (`docs/early-end-taken-back.md`, "Step 2"). When the person speaks again after an early end, what they go on to say carries, inside its activity just before its end: "The person paused and then went on: the request just before this one was cut off by that pause, and this is the rest of it. Answer all of it as one request." It goes together with any other note the worker gives that request (the name, the room).

Why the rest and not the whole question, which is what lamp-4ace answered as one: sending the piece's sound again is not possible. The transport takes no sound older than 2.5 s (`MAX_INPUT_AGE`), and the pizza question came in four pieces.

So the probe now asks exactly this note on the rest of a question: `rest-labelled` with a new `rest.wav` ("Japan?") replaces `resume-late`, still 15 requests. A test holds the voice's note and the probe's `REST_NOTE` to the same words. The probe's loader also reads the voice's own provider file as it is, ignoring the fields it does not use, as the first builder asked on #723.

**Verification folder:** none new; nothing was run against the service or on a lamp. Step 1's readings are in `docs/verification/early-end-probe-lamp-4ace-20261014/`. The tests:
- **Early-end session tests** (scripted service): when speech resumes 0.3 s after the end, and in "Lamp, stop." over an answer, the successor's wire is its sound, then the note, then its end.
- **The probe's six tests**, among them a provider file with the voice's other fields read, and a loose credential file still refused.

**On the lamp, smallest first** (`docs/early-end-taken-back.md`, "What to run on the lamp"):
1. Make `rest.wav` and run the probe once more, with the voice's own provider file. `rest-labelled` should answer Tokyo without answering "the capital of" on its own.
2. Only then the five pause scenes with `--early-end-ms 200`, against a run without it. The document has a table of what each scene should and should not do.

Most likely wrong there:
- the rest alone being weaker than the whole;
- a note arriving after the given-up answer has begun, under `kept-start`;
- thoughts in several pieces;
- pieces heard as another language.

**Gate**, on the M2 Max, on `f84889c91`. That is this branch rebased onto `lamp-voice` `e12a6cc83`, which brought #782's `continues` on the same `ProviderInput::Start`.
- Both fields are kept, each behind its own switch with its own reader:
  - `continues` (`LAMP_CUT_KEEPS_NAME`): the busy-room rule keeps the first part's call;
  - `continues_cut_off` (this branch, `--early-end-ms`): the note to the model.

  Every Start site names both, and each field's wire test is kept.
- The early-end fixture's `run()` is now `run_with_privacy_tolerance()` (`8bcde112d`); the two newest tests use it.
- fmt passes. clippy `-D warnings` passes on the 22 crates that are or use `lamp-msgs`.
- `lamp-gemini`: 256 passed.
- `lamp-voice` (`--no-fail-fast`, one thread): 1,241 passed and 1 failed. The failure, `native_head_replayed_receipt_and_changed_camera_grant_are_terminal` (a motor timing test, #739's family), ran while this Mac built two other branches. It passed alone 3 of 3.
- The workspace build passes.

**ARM64:** this pull request's run on `f84889c91`. Pull request runs skip the realtime group, which holds every `coordinator::tests::early_end` test (`.config/nextest.toml`), so those ran here on the Mac and run in full on `lamp-voice` after a merge.

title: lampOS: the privacy switch closes both microphones and the ring shows it, behind LAMP_PRIVACY_CONTROLS=on
body:
Closes #755

**Kind:** off unless set. The switch is `LAMP_PRIVACY_CONTROLS=on`, set in Controls, Voice and Ears together. Unset, `off` or any other value leaves all three exactly as they are on `lamp-voice`: Voice keeps reading chip 1 line 9 itself, and Ears keeps its old capture loop.

**What it does with the switch on**
- Controls reads the privacy slide on chip 1 line 9 (pull-up, LOW = muted) from an explicit `privacy` section in its pins file, and publishes it in `controls/state.privacy`, stamped with when the line was read. Controls grants no permission.
- Voice reads that instead of the GPIO and keeps its existing gate: evidence younger than 50 ms, and 60 ms of steady open before reopening. Its software mute stays separate; opening the slide never clears it.
- Voice gives Ears a short lease on `voice/privacy` (50 ms). Without a fresh lease Ears drops its own MIC1 handle and discards held samples. So both microphones close.
- The ring shows V1's dark-red breath while muted, from a separate ring worker that starts only after the active one has stopped.

**Off changes nothing** (host): Controls built at `5798f73d3` and at this branch gave byte-identical output files for the written hand fixture and the #711 strip fixtures, shadow and enabled, with the variable unset. The only stderr difference is one added usage line. `controls/state` JSON is unchanged when the field is empty. The Controls, Voice and Ears tests for unset/`off`/other values are in `crates/controls/tests/privacy_program.rs`, `crates/voice/tests/privacy_controls.rs` and `crates/ears/src/privacy/tests.rs`.

**Verification:** [docs/verification/privacy-switch-host-20261015](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/4c154fee3/lampOS/docs/verification/privacy-switch-host-20261015/README.md). Doc: [privacy-switch.md](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/9f1925af3/lampOS/docs/privacy-switch.md).

**Gate,** on Third's Intel i7-10700K Mac, macOS 26.6.2, Rust 1.96.0, at an earlier head of this same change (on `lamp-voice` `a28048886`; the native ARM64 run below covers the current head), build folder outside the repository:
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: one diff, in First's `crates/voice/src/agent_tasks.rs:396` (fixed on `lamp-voice` since), not in this change.
- `cargo clippy --offline --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --offline --workspace --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=1`: 4,506 passed, 3 failed, 34 ignored, 294 harnesses. The 3: `lamp-health`'s `a_part_that_is_expected_and_silent_or_has_gone_quiet_ends_show_with_3` (this Mac's disk is 91% full, so health warns first) and `wrong_arguments_print_the_usage_and_end_with_2_for_serve_and_64_for_show`, both failing on `a28048886` itself 3 times of 3; and `lamp-memory`'s usage test, which passed 5 of 5 alone. The usage tests lose a last stderr line through the log relay (below).
- On the same change at `5798f73d3` (the verification folder): 4,467 passed, 0 failed, 34 ignored.
- Host latency, injected switch read to a checked `controls/state` read back from the Bus, release build: first ~580 µs, p50 ~300 µs, p95 ~570 µs (target 50 ms). No real GPIO, microphone or ring in that number.

**Native ARM64:** run [38826274516](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/actions/runs/38826274516) green on this head `9f1925af3` (rebuilt onto `lamp-voice` `8cafa9893`, with #891: `docs/msgs.md` keeps both catalogue sentences; earlier rebuilds kept `msgs`' `selftest`, `privacy`, `memory_topics()`, `logging_topics()` and `privacy_topics()`, and merged the privacy worker's spawn into upstream's `later_tick`): 5,108 passed, 0 failed, one runner, Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64, the Linux-only `losing_controls_ends_the_real_worker_and_expires_its_lease_despite_current_allowed_authority` among them. Binaries, SHA-256:
- `lamp-controls` `7cd9886208c19dd6d33a7a4ee7e98ebd25486c0c42bb508b971c425c62b7d443`
- `lamp-voice` `96fa35b44e64328557c6781ed92c9f44a183138d483cef41e034761248977bbd`
- `lamp-ears` `914b76f8bcd246a104e17c2258c63313c918373c46656f01575a916298a48ba1`

Earlier: run 38800171243 green on `171289872` (4,971 passed); run 38770376188 green on `c047ce805` (4,824 passed); run 38756093472 green on `f0c55a49c` (4,737 passed); run 38746376142 green on `97dfbc78e` (4,675 passed); run 38728246092 attempt 3 green on `862fec7d0` (4,579 passed); run 38712595748 green on `4c154fee3` (4,569 passed).

**Since the first review** (all in the one commit): the test First asked for, `controls_stopping_with_the_slide_open_closes_both_microphones_within_50_ms` (fails if Ears keeps a permit 10 ms longer); the verification folder cut to one README; the reviewer's fix that a muted indication whose ring process never started is only logged and does not end the voice at the stable unmute (`a_ring_that_never_started_leaves_the_wait_to_open_without_its_light`, failing on the old behaviour), with a started writer still owing its black write and exit; and `service-privacy.md`/`ring-choreography.md` saying so.

**On lamp-4ace** ([privacy-switch.md](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/9f1925af3/lampOS/docs/privacy-switch.md#firsts-lamp-handoff) has the steps):
1. The minute with the switch off: install the new `lamp-controls`, `lamp-voice` and `lamp-ears`, keep the units and pins file as they are. Nothing should change.
2. Switch on: stop Voice and Ears first (Voice holds line 9 today), add the `privacy` section to the pins file, set `LAMP_PRIVACY_CONTROLS=on` in all three units, start Controls, then Voice and Ears.
3. Slide to mute at startup and while listening, thinking and speaking: `controls/state.privacy.muted=true`, `voice/privacy.permitted=false`, no MIC1 or MIC2 capture handle open, ring dark red. Slide back: the voice comes back with a fresh start, no old audio.

**Most likely wrong on the lamp:** the line's real polarity or wiring (pull-up means a loose wire reads as "not muted"), which ALSA device Ears really owns, a cold start missing the 50 ms freshness budget, and the ring's start/stop time. None of these is shown here; no lamp was used.

**For the reviewer:** this changes `crates/msgs` (a new optional `controls/state.privacy` field, skipped when empty, and a new `voice/privacy` topic) and Voice and Ears, so it is likely one for the first builder's minute.

**Found, not mine:** `lamp_ipc::log_relay` sometimes loses a process's last stderr lines on a quick exit: usage and error tests in health, memory, policy and Controls' `touch_program.rs` fail at random on `lamp-voice` itself, more often on a loaded machine. And on this Mac, processes started from under the repository's own `target/` run about 4× slower, so timed tests fail there; the gate used a build folder outside the repository. Both are in the verification README.

title: lampOS: a lock kept on each lamp as a 10-minute lease, so builders on any machine take turns at it (eighth-P1)
body:
Closes #833

**Kind:** changes nothing a lamp runs: a shell tool under `lampOS/tools/`, its test, and the rule in `joining.md`. No crate changed.

**What changed since 32d4c3253** (the reviewer's six findings and the first builder's lease, 18:54):
- A lease: `renew` every 5 min; a lock not renewed for 10 min (by the lamp's clock) has expired, the next take replaces it and appends the old one to `~/lamp.lock.log`; `status` shows the last renewal and "expired".
- Every step (look, take, renew, release) is one ssh call running one script on the lamp under `flock ~/.lamp.lock.mutex`, so check-and-remove can no longer interleave with a take.
- Holder and session compared as whole strings with `[ = ]`, no regular expressions (`session.1` cannot release `sessionX1`).
- The script's answers are its own exit codes (10/11/12); anything else, ssh's 255 included, is exit 3 "cannot ask", never "free" or "released".
- `run` releases only a lock it took itself; under a lock the same holder/session already hold it just runs the command. `run` renews while the command runs and stops the command if the lock is lost.
- Both scripts are mode 100755.
- `run` puts its command in a process group of its own and stops the whole group (TERM, KILL after 10 s) before releasing: when the command ends, when the lock is lost, and when no renewal has been confirmed for 540 s, counted from the start of the last confirmed call, with a hung renewal call killed with its own group. ssh gets a 15 s keepalive. (Reviewer 00:29, two P2s.)
- The jump-host example is `-J <host>` (P3).
- On the lamp, a failed write, rename, log append or remove exits 5 and nothing is announced: `try`/`acquire`/`run` do not take (and `run` does not start its command), `renew` and `release` exit 3 (reviewer 00:57).
- A lost lease is handled by the renewer itself: TERM to the command's group, KILL after 10 s, even while `run` is still waiting on a command that ignores TERM. A renewal call still running at any exit is stopped with every process under it, and waited for, before the release (reviewer 00:57). A `set -e` exit inside the EXIT trap, when the renewer was killed before its own trap was set, is fixed (found while testing: 1 in 100 `run -- true` exited 143 without releasing).
- A lock with no `renewed_epoch` (written by the older script) or a malformed one is dated by the file's modification time, not epoch 0. Found by nine on lamp-75c9 at 00:18:33, when its `try` replaced ten's live old-format lock.

**Test:** `lampOS/tools/lamp-lock-test.sh`, no lamp, a stand-in for ssh: 87 passed, 0 failed, six runs in a row; the cases since 71: a TERM-ignoring command killed within the grace after a lost lease, a command ending during a hung renewal, and take/run/renew/release on a lamp that cannot write its lock (on Linux x86_64). Covers the distinct-session case, transport down for status/release/renew/try, expiry and takeover, nested run, run under explicit acquire, renewal during run, and a lost lock stopping the command.

**Gate:** `bash -n` both scripts; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. ARM64 run: 38787716982 on `d0743159a`, green; d0743159a's predecessor d108ae0a6 was green, 38780019701; the previous one, 38776871505, failed only on `native_head_six_explicit_actions_prepare_profile_then_new_requests`, #739's family, which part 2 on `eighth/motor-clock` addresses). On lamp-75c9: `docs/verification/lamp-lock-lamp-75c9-20261016/`, four runs, lock files only; run 4 on this head (a TERM-ignoring worker killed after the grace, before the release); run 3 on this head's `run` (renewed every 2 s, a leftover worker stopped, released). Run 2 met nine's real lock and refused/waited correctly, but its hand-made expiry step (`renewed_epoch` set to 1 over ssh) hit nine's live lock and let a stand-in holder take and release it; nine was told at once. The README says so; a real-lamp test must not write the lock file by hand.

title: lampOS: a full look when asked what the lamp sees, behind --full-look and LAMP_LOOK_FULL (#836)
body:
Closes #836

**Kind:** off unless set. Two switches, turned on together: `lamp-eyes --full-look WIDTHxHEIGHT` (needs `--sight-file`) and `LAMP_LOOK_FULL=on` in the voice service. Without them nothing changes; the tests that show it:
- `eyes main::tests::a_full_look_is_off_unless_given_a_size_and_the_sight_file` (no flag: no size; the ask is not a permission) and `without_a_full_look_the_camera_opens_as_before_and_every_frame_is_kept` (`opened_at`, `keeps_working_frame`)
- `voice sight::tests::without_a_full_look_a_look_goes_at_once_with_the_old_note_and_asks_nothing` (no ask to the eyes, no wait, `LOOK_NOTE` unchanged, no worker flag)

**Touches the privacy path (camera) and the fifth's eyes crate**, so likely for the first builder.

## What changed

**eyes (fifth's crate, behind `--full-look`)** — `crates/eyes/src/full_look.rs`, `main.rs`
- The stream opens at the given size (e.g. 1280x960 MJPG) instead of 320x240; the detector already shrinks any frame to its 320x256. The working frame is no longer kept in the sight file.
- `{"look_full":ID}` on the existing `--permit-socket` asks for one still, marked with that id in a JPEG comment (`lamp-look ID`). It waits for the head to settle from `body/joint_states` (`bus.latest`, read every 50 ms): every head joint (`base_yaw`, `head_pitch`, `head_roll`) turning slower than 25 counts/s and staying within 6 counts of where it stopped, for 0.3 s, from the joints' actual positions and velocities; the commanded goal is not read (a resting head stands short of its goal and the body nudges its goals, so a goal rule never settled on lamp-4ace); a movement before the frame comes restarts the wait; capped at 2 s; no joint states = no wait. The still is the first frame after settling: passed through if a whole JPEG ≤ 64 KiB and ≤ 1024 wide, otherwise decoded, box-averaged down to 1024 wide, encoded at q85/75/65/50 until ≤ 64 KiB (`lamp_gemini::MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`). Written to the full-look file, removed after 15 s (the voice drops a look not begun 15 s after the lamp said it would look). No still within 2.5 s = none. One journal line: size, bytes, head wait, time to make. No picture logged.
- **No mode switch.** Following the fifth's warning (the 52e6 ZVCAI often fails to open again for 6–18 min after a close), the camera is never stopped/restarted for a still. One mode, opened once. If opening at the full size fails, the next try is 320x240, and the one after that the full size again (logged).
- New dependency: `jpeg-encoder =0.7.1` (pure Rust, no deps, MIT/Apache + IJG).

**body: no change.** The head's turn is the body's existing gaze (`--gaze-socket`) and turn-to-call (`--look-at-name on`). `body/joint_states` is enough to tell settled; the fifth's offered `settled` field is not needed.

**voice (behind `LAMP_LOOK_FULL=on`)** — `sight.rs` (`Look`), `coordinator.rs`, `body_link.rs`, `provider_worker.rs`, `speak_up.rs`, `main.rs`
- When the lamp's words ask to look ("Let me look"), the eyes are asked at once with a new id (`look_full_asked` in the record), so the settle and the still happen while the lamp is still saying it.
- The look turn waits until the eyes' file holds the still with that id, or at most 2.6 s (`look_full_still` in the record: ms after the ask, still there or not).
- The worker gets `--eyes-look-full` and takes a full look's still up to 15 s old (1 s otherwise).
- `LOOK_FULL_NOTE` adds: "If you cannot make out what they are showing you, say so plainly and ask them to hold it a bit closer to you; never guess what it might be."
- Each ask has its own id; the look takes the file only when its comment carries this ask's id (after review: a write time cannot tell a late still of a cancelled look from this one's). Otherwise the look goes with no picture and `NO_LOOK_NOTE`: no still, an earlier look's still, a cancelled look's still written late, or eyes without `--full-look` (no id; the two switches go together).

**docs:** `docs/eyes.md` ("A full look"), `docs/speaking-first.md` ("Taking a look").

## Host tests
- eyes `full_look`: only the exact ask counts; head still from joint states (only the head joints count); the still is the first frame after turning and settling (turn-then-capture ordering with fixture joint states); a head following a slow move with a count of lag is not still; a head that moves again before the frame is waited for again; a truly still head is taken; a head that never settles or no body still gets a still; a 1280x960 frame is made to fit 64 KiB; a small whole frame is passed through; box averaging.
- voice `sight`: switch off = unchanged; full look asks once per turn and waits for a still written after the ask; no still = goes after the wait; note has the unsure wording and the old note does not; a full look's still may be up to 15 s old; `--eyes-look-full` parsing. `body_link`: the exact datagram to the eyes.

## Working frame and still apart (for #873, option (a))
- With `--full-look`, the eyes keep writing the working frame to `--sight-file` exactly as before (each look, 0600, removed on close), shrunk from the full-size frame to 320x240 (`full_look::working`; a 320x240 fallback frame goes as it is). `lamp-policy --images` (#873) keeps a frame under 1 s old at any time.
- The still goes to a new `--full-look-file PATH` (0600, id-tagged, kept 15 s, removed on close). `--full-look` and `--full-look-file` go together and the file must differ from the sight file.
- The voice reads the still from `LAMP_EYES_FULL_LOOK_FILE` (a full look needs it and `LAMP_LOOK_FULL=on`); the worker gets that path as `--eyes-look` plus `--eyes-look-full`. Without the switches, unchanged.
- Cost: the full-size frame is decoded a second time each look for the working frame (marked `ponytail:`; measure ms a look on the lamp).

## Camera bounds raised (camera crate, found on lamp-52e6)
- `lamp_camera::MAX_HEIGHT` 720 → 960: 1280x960 was refused before the device was touched ("InvalidData None").
- `lamp_camera::MAX_FRAME_BYTES` 2 MiB → 4 MiB: the camera answers 1280x960 MJPG with a 2,457,600-byte buffer, refused at SetFormat. The eyes' frame buffer grows 2 → 4 MiB.
- The voice's own camera config is pinned to its old bounds (720 high, 2 MiB), so the voice is unchanged; `--full-look` refuses at start any size over the camera's bound. Host tests with the exact negotiated mode (1280x960 MJPG, bytesperline 0, sizeimage 2,457,600) and the 14 listed sizes.

## Lamp-52e6 verification
`docs/verification/full-look-lamp-52e6-20261015/` (the coordinator's runs, from `4956b840f`; ten objects drawn full-screen on a MacBook about a metre away, asked "Hey Lamp, what am I showing you?"):
- Named **6 of 10** in their own trial with the full look, plus **one ambiguous** (a banana answer that came late, in the next trial's window, not counted); pictures 59.8–65.1 KB. Before: **4 of 10** with the 320x240 working frame (15.9–16.7 KB), scored the same way.
- `look_full_asked` → `look_full_still`: **622–1,060 ms** (median about 800 ms). That is ask to the **coordinator accepting** the still, which happens only once "Let me look." has ended, not ask to capture; the capture's own time was not kept. The eyes logged a head wait of 0 ms for each look, so settling was not the cause.
- Time to the answer's first word was **not kept**: request-bound first-word timestamps are missing; the README gives the session's unbound look_asked → next provider_first_audio gap (2.0–3.6 s) as an unverified observation only. None of this is comparable with the ~300 ms aim yet.
- Eyes at 1280x960: **87 ms a look** (64–81 ms at 320x240).

## Not shown
Objects held up by a person, the head turning toward a person (nobody was in view), lamp-4ace. `--full-look` and `LAMP_LOOK_FULL` are not added to any deploy unit.

## Gate (macOS host)
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean

title: lampOS: --zone system in Expression, Memory and the policy (#820)
body:
Closes #820

Homes outside Vietnam change their clocks. `--zone system` (or `--zone America/New_York`) takes the zone's offset at each moment, in the three parts that took `--utc-offset-minutes`. That flag is unchanged; the two together are refused. Head `b3c3ca47e`, on `lamp-voice` `fc5a7c792` (merges cleanly onto `48b3737d5`). One commit per part, so each owner can read theirs:

1. **`lamp-local-time`** (new, Third's) and **Expression** (Third's), `6df38a9ce`, `1c6cf42c1`, `a375c97cb`. One reader for all three.
   - `--zone system` follows `/etc/localtime`, which setup points at the phone's zone by renaming a new link over it, often after the parts have started.
   - At every reading it looks at the link (even when its target is gone), where the link points, the file it leads to, and the name file `/etc/timezone` (three `stat` calls and a `readlink`). It reads the zone again only when one of them changed, so a new zone counts from the next reading with no restart (Second's point 2; the reviewer's first #844 point).
   - A change that cannot be read keeps the last zone. A zone that cannot be read at start ends the start, never a silent UTC.
   - Night in Expression stays at the same clock hours across a change.
2. **Memory** (the seventh's, please read), `9df579365`, `a355e3ef9`, `b3c3ca47e`. `--zone` in place of the offset; the journal day turns at local midnight in summer too.
   - The memory-across-days store keeps its days by the local calendar, as the journal store does: today's local day minus the days kept (`Day::before`), so a 23- or 25-hour day loses nothing early (the reviewer's second point).
   - The start line says `zone=` instead of `utc_offset_minutes=` only when `--zone` is given.
   - Memory's new rule links (upstream) are kept, and their records are inserted with the zone.
3. **The policy** (the second's, as agreed on #820), `96dcdf201`. `--zone`; only `hour` in the progress question uses it, the zoned hour of the decision's moment. With neither flag it stays null.

**Off changes nothing:** no unit passes `--zone`, so every part runs as before. Switching the units over is First's (`docs/setup.md` says so).

**Tests:**
- New York's 2026 changes (8 March, 1 November): the hour, the minute, and the 23- and 25-hour days.
- Vietnam by name equals 420 all year.

- Memory: journal files at local midnight in January and July. The memory-across-days store keeps a day across both clock changes (`keep_days` 1: Oct 31 stays at Nov 1 23:30 local, Mar 7 goes at Mar 9 00:30 local), and after reopening.
- Policy: 23:00 in New York in winter and summer.

title: lampOS: the head pads, end to end (#711)
body:
For #711: the head pads, end to end, as the owner chose (`docs/creature.md` "Touch", First's 19:28 direction). **Draft:** it grows one step at a time; the plan is on #711.

**Step 1, Controls and msgs (`534c704c0`), only with `--touch`:** the head, both pads as one hand.

| The hand | Speaking | Quiet | Asleep |
|---|---|---|---|
| Touch, qualified at 20 ms | Stop | Notice (nothing asked) | nothing |
| Tap, let go before 0.5 s | Attend | Attend | Wake |
| Kept 1 s | Stroke (lean in) | Stroke | nothing |
| Kept 3 s | Sleep | Sleep | nothing |

- A hand that stays is one hand: released acquisitions shorter than `HEAD_GAP_US` (150 ms, authored; to be set from lamp-4ace's recording, asked on #711) don't end it, because V1's TTP223 pads can pulse under a resting hand. Only an unbroken 20 ms run qualifies a touch.
- `touch_state.held_us` counts through those gaps: it is the countdown for the eye.
- Letting go after a Stroke asks nothing; it was affection.
- `TouchEngine::set_head_pushed`: a contact that overlaps a push from the body asks nothing more. A Stop already sent stands, because waiting to feel a push would break the 150 ms stop. The runtime input waits on the fifth's signal (#703).
- New `TouchIntent::Notice`. Head Touch no longer offers Attend or Wake. Only Controls' own `--touch` path and its checker read head events, and no unit passes `--touch`.

**Off changes nothing:** lamps run Controls without `--touch` (the head means Pet there, unchanged).

**Gate (step 1),** Third's Intel i7 Mac, macOS 26.6.2, Rust 1.96.0:
- fmt clean.
- Workspace clippy `-D warnings` clean.
- Linux ARM64 clippy clean for Controls and msgs.
- Controls, msgs and Setup, run one at a time: 481 passed. The 4 that failed were three `touch_program` tests under load (they passed 2 of 2 alone), and a replay test whose head hold was too short for the new 1 s Stroke; it was lengthened, and it passes.

**Step 1b (`c237b5c3b`):** `head_qualify_ms` (20), `head_tap_min_ms` (120) and `head_gap_ms` (150) are settings in the touch pins file, to be sized from First's recording. A lone edge under 120 ms (one was seen at 19:25) never asks the lamp to listen.

**Step 2, Voice, behind `LAMP_HEAD_TOUCH=on`:**
- `e274316f5`: a head touch stops the lamp while it says its answer (reply audio or playback), through the button's `hand::cancel` (`hand_control_cancel`, `reason: head_stop`). While quiet or thinking it is only noted (`head_touch_noticed`). Host probe, a real bus to the voice's poll, 3 × 100 on Third's Mac: medians 1.8–2.1 ms, p95 2.7 ms. One earlier run once lost a touch for 2 s; not seen again.
- `7f724dff8`: a head tap is a call for 6 s in the attention rule. The provider worker takes taps from the bus beside the name, so it needs `LAMP_BUS=on`.
- Voice gate, Third's Mac: clippy clean.
  - Hand-control, attention, bus and composed coordinator tests pass.
  - The full Voice run under load had 36 failures: 19 are the motor fixtures (#739); the rest are process and child timing tests that pass one at a time. Three provider-worker tests fail the same way on plain `lamp-voice` under 4 threads.

**Step 3, Expression, behind `serve --head-touch`** (`c5539ee7b`): it leans into a hand kept on the head (pitch -0.015, roll 0.02 rad, in over 0.5 s, out over 0.6 s), only awake and with the body free. A 3 s hold puts it to sleep, by day too; a tap wakes it. 235 Expression tests pass.

**Step 4, the ring's countdown, behind `LAMP_HEAD_TOUCH=on`** (`e2b8dcd80`): the ring worker reads the head's `held_us` from the bus every 50 ms (`ring_head.rs`, worker flag `--head-touch`). From 1 s to 3 s of a held hand the whole face dims to 15 %, eased, and brightens again when the hand goes; it is never dark. 120 ring tests pass on my Mac. `run_continuous` is Linux-only, so its build is checked by the ARM64 run.

**Rebuilt** on `lamp-voice` `71a15e75d` (head `2a3a5e278`, then the countdown). The voice's stop now sits beside upstream's capture-gap cancel: reason `head_stop`, and the gap's reset runs only for a gap.

**Native ARM64:** run [38769234167](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/actions/runs/38769234167) green on `ce7393af2` (rebuilt onto `lamp-voice` `b60062b86`): 4,763 passed, 0 failed.

**Step 5, the body's push** (`24dae4905`): `--touch` Controls reads `body/hand` (#848) every 20 ms, before each step's head samples. Only a fresh message from the body that says `pushed` counts, so a stopped body never silences the head. A change is recorded as `head_pushed` for replay.

**Rebuilt** on `lamp-voice` `3b146029d` with no conflicts. Controls 393 passed on Third's Mac; clippy clean on macOS and Linux ARM64. The new ARM64 run starts from this push.

**Step 6, sleep is the software mute with the reason `sleep`** (First's decision on #711, 21:24), needing `LAMP_HEAD_TOUCH=on` **and** `--controls-mute` in the voice:
- `3c5e91077` (Controls, msgs): `MuteRecord` gets an optional `reason`, written only while muted, so old records read as before. `Receiver::request_sleep` takes a head Hold; `Receiver::request_wake` takes a head Tap. The wake only marks the clear pending, and the quiet owner prepares, saves and commits it exactly as for the button's second hold.
  - A tap never opens a privacy mute.
  - A hand that began before the last change asks nothing.
  - A button hold makes a sleep a privacy mute.
  - A reboot keeps the reason.
  - New `VoiceMute` on `voice/mute` (latest, every 1 s, kept 3 s).
- `1a25c0566` (Voice): a 3 s hold sleeps as any mute does (`hand_control_cancel` and `service_cycle_muted` say `head_sleep`). A tap in the wait wakes it once the clear is saved. The one controls pump says `voice/mute` on change and every second, in a conversation and in the wait.
- `a26b6ef39` (Expression `--head-touch`): asleep while `voice/mute` says sleep, whatever else calls (a tap the voice did not take, the name, a touch, a reminder, a face). It wakes when the voice opens. With no word from the voice for 3 s, the head acts as before.

**Step 7, the "hm?"** (`a7467a9ed`, behind `LAMP_HEAD_TOUCH=on`): a tap on a quiet lamp plays a soft hum of its own, as its own turn, like the self-test's tone (`commit_sound_turn`, `SpeechOrigin::HeadCue`).
- **The sound:** two tones rising, 330 and 415 Hz with soft overtones, 300 ms in all, -35 dBFS RMS. That is the lamp's speech taken as about -20 dBFS, less 15 dB; it is not measured yet. `LAMP_HEAD_TAP_CUE_DBFS` tunes it by ear.
- **When:** never more than once in 30 s, and only quiet, listening ready, microphone allowed and no look owed. Never after a touch that stopped speech.
- **Trace:** each tap writes `head_tap_cue` with `plays` and `why`. The first-chunk row is now named for what plays, so the self-test tone's is `selftest_tone_attempted` (it was `failure_notice_attempted`).
- **Speed:** Controls raises a tap 150 ms (`head_gap_ms`) after the hand lifts. The hum's decision to its first chunk sent to the speaker took 2.3 ms median and 2.7 ms p95 on Third's Mac (ignored probe). Tap to the speaker's write on a lamp is not measured.

**Step 8, the eye and the head at a tap** (First's design on #711, 05:05: one gesture from the one tap event, behind the same switches):
- `16f06ee67` (voice ring, `LAMP_HEAD_TOUCH=on`): the ring worker reads head taps from `controls/touch` on every 2 ms tick and draws rest every 25 ms. At rest the resting face becomes the listening face for 2 s (`TAP_LISTENS_US`, as long as a call waits on lamp-4ace, #891). If nothing comes it settles back, most of the way in half a second, not snapping. The hum's own turn is drawn as that listening face from the pass that admits it (`RingFrame::listening`), so the face comes with the hum. Other turns' faces are unchanged.
- `2ca295034` (Expression `--head-touch`): on an awake lamp a tap lifts the head (pitch -0.035 rad), more toward a face seen high in the picture and less for one low (0.025 rad at the edge). It comes in over 150 ms, holds 2 s and longer while someone speaks, and goes out over 0.5 s. Never while the lamp thinks or speaks, never a turn of the body (no gaze is sent, which would turn the base). A tap that wakes it is a wake, not a look-up.

**Rebuilt** on `lamp-voice` `48b3737d5` (`docs/msgs.md` kept both rows; the coordinator fixture names upstream's new `cut_keeps_name`). Head `a7467a9ed`; it merges cleanly onto `d60124f82`. The SHAs in steps 1–5 above are from before the rebuilds; the commits are the same, in the same order.

**Gate at `a7467a9ed`**, Third's Intel i7 Mac, macOS 26.6.2, Rust 1.96.0, build outside the repository:
- fmt clean, `cargo metadata --locked` clean.
- clippy `-D warnings` clean for msgs, Controls, Expression and Voice; Linux ARM64 clippy clean for msgs, Controls and Expression.
- msgs, Controls, Expression and Voice, 4 at a time: 2,131 passed and 4 failed at `a4747a401`. The Voice alone at `a7467a9ed`: 1,405 passed and 4 failed. The 4 are the same reminder tests both times (`provider_worker::tests::reminders` and `reminder_roundtrip`), which this PR does not touch. All 76 reminder tests pass one at a time.

**Native ARM64:** run [38825302140](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/actions/runs/38825302140) green on `4ddea3ebb` (the review fix, on `8cafa9893`): 5,062 passed, 0 failed. Earlier: run 38817615121 on `2ca295034` (4,990 passed); run 38811863826 on `a7467a9ed` (the hum, 4,977 passed) and run 38808900420 on `a4747a401` (the sleep).

**Gate at `2ca295034`** (on `lamp-voice` `48b3737d5`, merges cleanly onto `578288f88`), Third's Mac: fmt clean; clippy `-D warnings` clean for Voice and Expression, Linux ARM64 clippy clean for Expression. Voice and Expression, 4 at a time: 1,649 passed and 6 failed. The 6 are provider-worker timing tests this PR does not touch (the reminder tests, `a_sound_heard_as_another_language…`, `review_a_name_heard_after_a_requests_sound_ended…`), and all pass one at a time. New tests: the face at rest after a tap and its slow settle, the ring reading only Controls' head taps, the hum's turn drawn as the listening face in every phase, and Expression's look-up (timing, toward a face, held while someone speaks, none while it speaks or when the tap wakes it).

Part of #841 (the other builders' steps remain). Design: https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/issues/841#issuecomment-6193362903

**Kind:** off unless set. Switch: `LAMP_ONBOARDING=on` and an absolute `LAMP_ONBOARDING_FILE` in the voice unit. Then the coordinator runs the walk and passes `--onboarding-file` to the provider worker, which declares `setup_step` and `redo_setup`. Without both, no function is declared, no file is read or written, and no turn is begun. Pinned by `tools::tests::without_the_onboarding_switch_nothing_changes` (same declared list and routes without the flag; a relative path is refused) and `onboarding::tests::the_switch_is_on_only_with_on_and_an_absolute_file`.

**What it does** (`crates/voice/src/onboarding.rs`, a hook in the coordinator's loop beside the hello): a runner that owns order and timing. Each step begins as a written note (`ProviderInput::Written`), only at rest, with a face in front of the lamp and not paused. Every line is the model's.

| Step | State | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 1 where you sit | **built**: largest fresh face on `humans/faces/tracked` ≥ 0.14 height, centre within 0.25 of the middle, held 3 s. Guidance notes (no face / closer / turn me toward you) after 8 s quiet; failed after 60 s with a note on what to do later; framing kept | seventh |
| 2 who you are | **built**: the model asks their name, then `remember_my_face` after a clear yes, and reports with `setup_step` | seventh |
| 3 how you sound | placeholder (`not_available`, unspoken) | fourth (#753 follow-up) |
| 4 touch | placeholder | third (#711) |
| 5 privacy | placeholder | third (#795) |
| 6 giving way | placeholder: the voice can't tell whether the body runs `--limp on` | fifth (#780) |
| 7 preferences | **built**: quiet hours and greeting, kept as rules. Kept with `keep_rule` (#813, merged in #822) when the provider worker has both `LAMP_MEMORY_DAYS=on` and `LAMP_MEMORY_RULES=on`; with either off or the legacy memory, the model keeps them with `remember` | seventh |

Results: `LAMP_ONBOARDING_FILE` (JSON, 0600, coordinator the only writer). The worker appends the model's reports to `FILE.told`. These move to lamp-settings once #808 merges. Redo: "let's redo the setup" → `redo_setup` clears the file. A step that is never reported fails after 90 s plus 20 s of quiet. An empty room for 30 s or the keeper's pause drops the step being led, and it is asked again later. The hello is not said while a step is being led. Docs: new `docs/onboarding.md`, linked from `speaking-first.md` and `memory.md`.

**Host tests** (`onboarding::tests`, scripted room and face): steps walked in order and kept across a restart; a step skipped and the walk redone; a failing step saying what to do and moving on (step 1 by measurement, step 2 by timeout); the pause and an empty room stopping the step being led; the nearest face as framing. **Kind:** off unless set. It uses the same switch as #858 (`LAMP_ONBOARDING=on` and an absolute `LAMP_ONBOARDING_FILE`). With the switch off nothing here runs, and #858's no-change tests still hold.

**1. The body says it too.** A step that ends done asks the body for one move. It uses the path the answers' nods already take: `BodyLink::gesture`, `{"gesture":…}` on `LAMP_BODY_MOOD_SOCKET`.
- `where_you_sit` gets a nod, `who_you_are` a greeting, and any later step a nod.
- Skipped or failed steps get no move.
- With no body, or while the keeper's pause is set, nothing is sent and the move is not saved for later.
- Each move is recorded as `body_gesture_asked` with `"why":"onboarding"`.
- The body has no lean clip (its clips are nod, headshake, greeting, laugh, shy, stretching, idle), so the greeting stands in for First's "pleased lean". A lean would be the fifth's to add.

**2. A step that was not ready, offered later.** A step kept as `not_available` is offered again when a later voice build has it.
- Only after the walk is over, at a rest with someone there, and never in the middle of another step.
- Once offered, it is led to its end like any other step.
- Offered but not finished (they walked off, or the pause): it is offered again no sooner than a day later (`offered_at_unix_s` in the onboarding file).
- Whether a step is available is fixed per build (`Step::available`). The placeholder steps get a placeholder note ("one more thing I can do now"); each owner words their own step's note.

**Host tests** (`onboarding::tests`):
- `a_step_done_asks_the_body_for_one_move_and_a_skip_for_none`
- `a_step_that_was_not_available_is_offered_once_a_day_when_it_is`: not offered by the same build; offered by a later one after the walk; led while being led; not offered again the same day after the person leaves; offered again a day later, and kept as done.

title: lampOS: lamp-policy-replay compares decision models on the logged decisions, and lamp-policy --images asks again with the eyes' frame, both in shadow
body:
Part of #871:
- **item 1:** `lamp-policy-replay`, which asks the Policy's logged decisions again of Jev 1.13 and 1.14 (running on lamp-4ace since 23:18);
- **item 3, built and to be measured:** `lamp-policy --images`, which asks each attention question again with the eyes' frame;
- **for the switch:** `lamp-policy-replay --again … --refit`, which tells whether a model loses only because the weights were fitted to another model's answers.

#871 stays open for the measurements and the switch.

**Kind:** a tool run by hand, and `--images`, off unless set and shadow. Without `--images`, the Policy is as before:
- `main` goes through `policy::run_with_extras`, which with no pictures is `run_inner` exactly as before;
- a request without a picture is written as before; the only change on that path is that the write counts its bytes (`talk`), and a write that fails on a kept connection is retried exactly as before;
- `attention::Context` can be read back from the log (`Deserialize`);
- `names_the_lamp` only counts and decides nothing;
- a request without a picture is byte for byte as before (the pinned body test).

**`lamp-policy-replay`** (`docs/policy.md`, "Another model, asked the same questions again"):
- It reads `decisions-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` for the days given (UTC days).
- For each attention decision it asks each model given (up to four), one after the other, paced: the state text rebuilt from the logged `context` by the same `attention::state_text`, with the same seven questions. Each model's answers become a choice by the same weights.
- **It prints no words.** One line per decision: place and moment, room, conversation, name heard; the kinds of what was heard (`words`, `names_lamp`, `other_language`); the day's choice; the label if given; each model's choice, probability, `took_ms` and dated name, or why it failed.
- **Then a summary per model:**
  - answered, and `took_ms` p50/p95/max;
  - its choices;
  - how often it chose as the log did;
  - how often it did what should have happened, overall and for named requests, a busy room and another language;
  - then how often each two models chose alike.
- **Labels** are given by moment: `{"at_unix_ms": N, "should": "answer"|"stay_quiet"}`. `--again` counts an earlier run's lines with labels, without asking again.
- **A caveat in the summary:** the weights were fitted to jev-1.13's answers, and 1.14's answers go through them as they are. Each line therefore keeps each model's seven raw answers (numbers only).
- **`--refit`** (with `--again`): for each model, the weights fitted again to its own seven answers, the quiet room, the conversation and the name heard (logistic regression, weights pulled to zero as scikit-learn's default `C = 1`), on half the labelled lines, counted on the other half; 200 halves from one seed, the same for every model. Beside it, the run's own choices (the day's weights) on the same halves. One more line, `refit_summary`: mean right overall, named, busy room, other language, answered-not-for-the-lamp and ignored-for-the-lamp, for both; and the weights fitted on every label, to be read only. It needs a run with answers (`28a38cbb1` on), at least 20 labelled lines a model, and changes nothing the lamp does.

**`lamp-policy --images MODEL [--sight-file PATH]`** (`docs/policy.md`, "The lamp's picture with the question"):
- **The askings:** as each attention question is sent, a thread of its own, if free, asks `MODEL` twice at once on two connections. Without the picture it asks the seven questions as sent; with it, the state names the picture and five questions are added (faces the lamp, absorbed, talking to another, asks with a look, away). One line goes to `pictures-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`.
- **Never waited for:** the decision doesn't wait, and an utterance that comes while the thread is busy is passed over.
- **The picture:**
  - It is the eyes' newest frame, by the voice's rule: the eyes keep it only while the microphone may listen, and it must be at most 1 s old and at most 64 KiB.
  - It is made 640×480 for TypeSafe's least side of 256, sent as `assets` with `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true` on that request only, and written nowhere.
- **Taken at the moment of writing** (the reviewer's 00:10 and 00:38 findings): the frame is read when the request is written, after any looking up and connecting, and again for another connection; no frame then, nothing is written (`withdrawn`).
- **Sent means some of it went** (the reviewer's 01:13 finding): each try's delivery is told (`Partly(n)`, `Uncertain`, `Answered`); the line says `sent` if any try went, whatever came after, with `delivery`, `tries` and `withdrawn`.
- **Counted:** `lamp-policy-replay --pictures --log-dir … --days … [--labels …]` gives each asking's p50/p95, failures by kind and how often it was right, both on the same lines (a frame sent and both chose), delivery counts, and each picture question's yes beside the eyes' own `facing`. Each label goes once to the line nearest it within 3 s; contradicting labels at one moment are refused.

**Tests:**
- `crates/policy/src/replay/tests.rs`: the log read with each line's place; kinds ("Voglio mangiare sushi." as another language with no accented letter); each model asked exactly the day's text and choosing by the same weights; no words in a line; the counts; labels; counting again.
- `crates/policy/tests/replay_program.rs`: the program against a service played on this machine. Two models are asked in turn, the state sent equals the day's, and nothing heard is printed, on stdout or stderr.
- Pictures:
  - `src/decide/tests.rs`: the asset and the header.
  - `src/pictures/tests.rs`: the frame rule; 320×240 made 640×480; too small or too large refused; the state and the twelve questions.
  - `tests/pictures.rs`: the two askings against a played service, only one carrying the picture, the picture in no line, nothing asked with no frame, and the thread passing over while busy.
  - `tests/program.rs`: the program with `--images` publishes its decision as before and writes the picture's line.
  - `src/replay/tests.rs`: the picture lines counted against labels, each label once to its nearest line, contradicting labels refused, a picture that went counted as sent and both askings on the same lines.
  - `src/decide/tests.rs`: the frame of the moment of writing (removed, closed and reopened, replaced), and each request's delivery told.
  - `src/pictures/tests.rs`: the reviewer's 01:13 case: written whole on a kept connection closed unanswered, then withdrawn, told as sent.
- Refit: `src/replay/refit/tests.rs` (a model on another scale done badly by the day's weights and as well as the other once fitted to its own answers; a run without answers not fitted; the weights found from examples drawn from known ones; the same halves every time) and `tests/replay_program.rs` (`--again --refit` end to end).

**Gate** on the M2 Max, on `49c493727` (on `lamp-voice` `29b8e2232`, with #881):
- fmt passes.
- clippy `-D warnings` passes on the 23 crates that are or use `lamp-msgs`.

- The workspace build passes.

**With #883:** both change `crates/policy/src/main.rs` and `policy.rs`. Put together on today's `lamp-voice` they were gated on the M2 Max (`58e5b611f`: msgs 89, policy 193, voice 1,368 passed); whichever merges second is rebased onto the first at once.

title: lampOS: a due hello asks the policy on voice/arrival with LAMP_HELLO_ASKS_POLICY=on, and lamp-policy --hello answers, acting with --act hello
body:
For #856 (the second half of #752), agreed by the first builder on #856 at 00:02: the hello on arrival asks the Policy. #856 stays open for the lamp's sessions; acting comes only after them.

**Kind: off unless set.**
- **Voice:** `LAMP_HELLO_ASKS_POLICY=on`. Without it there is no `voice/arrival` publisher and no subscription. The hello is the fixed rule's, on the very tick it is due, and the session record and journal are as before (tests).
- **Policy:** `lamp-policy --hello` asks in shadow; `--act hello` acts. Without `--hello` there is no subscription and the diagnostics are unchanged.
- **Bus:** `Decision` gets an optional `arrival`, left out when empty, so every existing message stays byte for byte the same (a test).

**What it does** (`docs/speaking-first.md`, "Asking the policy (#752)"):
1. A due, ready hello publishes `voice/arrival` with:
   - an arrival number;
   - minutes away, seconds there, seconds of quiet;
   - minutes since the last hello.

   No image, no face, no identity.
2. The voice holds the hello up to 2 s for the Policy's decision about that number:
   - `say_now`, acting: said as before, still only with `LAMP_SPEAK_FIRST=on`, and by name for someone the lamp knows. The Policy is never told the name.
   - `wait`, acting: not said, and recorded (`hello_due` with `"policy":"wait"`).
   - A decision in shadow, or none within 2 s: today's rule.
3. The Policy asks Jev two questions, `welcome` and `intrusive`, with the progress question's room state plus facing. Asking is capped at 1.5 s.
4. Hard rules answer `wait` at once, without asking the model: never while anyone talks, and the voice's 20-minute limit.
5. It keeps the keeper's pause (#777): while the lamp is paused, no hello is begun or asked about. The hello's session is `unasked_session(&cloud, paused)`, as the fixed rule's is.
6. It counts how often the lamp spoke up unasked in the last hour from `voice/state`, which feeds the hard rule and `intrusive`. The reviewer's findings on this PR set three rules:
   - Whether a turn was asked for is decided at its start and kept until it ends. A turn the lamp began itself (its first `thinking` or `speaking` with nobody listened to in the 10 s before) is counted once, at its first sound, however often it speaks.
   - An answer whose first sound is slow (up to 30 s) is never counted.
   - In shadow, the voice's own greeting for a hello chosen just before is that same hello, counted once, or as chosen if it never makes a sound.

**The cost to a person:** the hello waits for the Policy.
- On the Mac, against a stand-in judge that answers at once, it was held a median of 22 to 32 ms, at most 38 ms (`docs/verification/hello-asks-host-20261015`).
- With Jev it is about Jev's time. The session record's `hello_policy` line says `waited_ms` for every hello, from the moment it was due to the answer, so the lamp's own cost can be read straight off it.

**Gate** on the M2 Max, on `589e904b1` (on `lamp-voice` `d60124f82`), in a build folder of its own:
- fmt passes. clippy `-D warnings` passes on the 24 crates that are or use `lamp-msgs`.
- `lamp-policy` 175 passed (2 ignored), 0 failed.
- `lamp-msgs` and `lamp-voice` are unchanged since `b89c2e260`, where they passed 95 and 1,410 (8 ignored), 0 failed.
- The workspace build passes.

**On lamp-4ace from tomorrow morning, in shadow** (the first builder's plan on #856):
1. Set `LAMP_HELLO_ASKS_POLICY=on` and `lamp-policy --hello`, without `--act hello`. The owner turns the lamp back to the seat before 11:00.
2. After the 11:00 and 16:00 sessions, read the `hello_due` and `hello_policy` lines (`waited_ms`) and the Policy's `welcome` and `intrusive` answers. 1 s late is fine; 3 s isn't. The cap is 2 s.

Most likely wrong there:
- Jev's time for the two questions with the progress state, which is longer than the attention question's. That would show as `waited_ms` near 1.5 s.
- An arrival the eyes see but the hello's rule never makes due: nothing is asked then. It is the same rule as today, so it would show as no `hello_due` at all.

**After this, not in it:** `memory/rules` (#813, merged today) carries what a person asked about speaking first (`quiet`, `quiet_mornings`). It fits as one more hard rule for the hello: asked never to speak first, `wait`.

title: lampOS: with LAMP_SPOKEN_TO=on the lamp answers only what was said to it, in every room (#829 step 2)
body:
Part of #829: step 2, **the lamp speaks when spoken to**. This is the first builder's judgement (#829, 22:13), with their two tests (02:00) and their day scene (02:39). It closes nothing.

**Kind: off unless set.** `LAMP_SPOKEN_TO=on` in the voice's environment. The coordinator passes the worker `--spoken-to`, right after `--name-in-passing-ignored`. Nothing changes without `LAMP_ATTENTION`.

**What it does, in every room:** an answer is played only when something shows the lamp was spoken to:
- its name, in the text (`called`, or `called_by_name` with `LAMP_NAME_IN_PASSING=ignored`) or heard by `lamp-name` in the sound;
- a face turned to the lamp. The eyes are now read for every answer, not only in a busy room;
- a conversation with the lamp going on (`going_on`, 45 s, as today);
- someone close to the lamp and turned to it spoke (`LAMP_ADDRESSED=on`);
- the lamp began the turn itself.

Otherwise the answer is held ("nobody spoke to the lamp: …"), and so is every lamp action it calls for. The call is answered and never reaches the executive, as in a busy room today.

**The day scene** (#829, 02:39). One person alone, straight after the two-person scenes, was shut out for good: each held line counted as more talk, so the room stayed busy. Under the same switch:
- **Only talk between people makes a room busy** (`room_told.rs`). A request whose answer the rule held is not talk, as a sound is not. Busy ends 3 minutes after the last talk, whatever one person says meanwhile; today it ends only after 5 minutes with nothing heard at all.
- **The lamp's news is replied to.** The first thing said within 3 minutes of a turn the lamp began itself (a task's news, a reminder) is played, once, in every room. The 3 minutes start when that turn's first sound is handed on to the coordinator, owner-checked and credited (`Attention::spoke`, in the worker's credited send). An own turn that ends silent, is cancelled before any sound, or whose sound a cancellation drops while it waits for credit, opens none (the reviewer's P2s at 05:11 and 06:17). The first thing judged after the news takes the window, whatever path judges it, a checked short sound included (the reviewer's P2 at 07:12).
- **A question about the lamp's own work is for it.** "task", "reminder", "timer" or "alarm", within 10 minutes of the lamp's news or of it starting a task, a timer or a reminder.
- A room not yet known, as after the voice starts, is quiet after 5 minutes with no talk between people (the first builder at 05:46: `room/state` said "unknown" all night).
- Not done: telling one voice from two. That needs the same-voice part (#865) running on the lamp. Until then, a different person's new line within 45 s of the lamp's last words rides on that conversation (the first builder at 06:15).

**A reply to someone called by name is not the lamp's** (#829, the first builder at 05:02). In scene 4, Samantha asked "Daniel, are you coming to the meeting at two?", and Daniel answered her "Yes, give me five minutes." He was in a conversation with the lamp, so it set a timer. With the switch, a line that comes within 10 s after one that called someone other than the lamp by name is that person's reply (`addresses_someone_else`, `ANOTHER_REPLY_US`).
- "Called by name" means a capitalised name set off by a comma, opening the line or closing it, that isn't the lamp's name, a word the service writes for it, or a word like "Okay,".
- For that line only the lamp's name counts: not the conversation, the news, the work question, or a face. A short sound let through and checked (#800) is held the same way (the reviewer's P2 at 06:06).

**The name needs no face** (#829, 03:29, from #908's run at 03:28). In a busy room, "Hey Lamp, turn your volume down a little." was held: the name was heard in the sound, and nobody was turned to the lamp. With the switch, a request whose sound had the name is played in a busy room too. The cost is the busy form's own reason for that hold: `lamp-name` hears the name in people's talk now and then (17 times from 07:45 to 13:02 on 14 October, at 0.903–0.997), and each of those now lets an answer out.

**What it would have held on lamp-4ace** (15 Oct first-output records, 13:01–16:07, 69 decisions): 4 of the 25 answers that played had no sign. Two were one-word sounds in a room not known to be busy. Two were the rest of a call the lamp cut at its comma (#782); with `LAMP_CUT_KEEPS_NAME=on` (#853) those keep the call's text and play. In a room not known to be busy the records have no face, so 4 is the most it could have held.

**Its cost: "Lamp, …" from someone not facing the lamp.** The service seldom writes the name. Of the calls played to the lamps from 12 to 16 October (1,722 scenario files), the text showed the call for 84 of 769 "Lamp, …" and 242 of 1,415 "Hey Lamp, …". `lamp-name` hears "Hey Lamp, …" (12 of 12 with the lamp quiet) but not "Lamp," alone (the first builder, #828, 02:05). So with the switch, "Lamp, …" said with nobody facing the lamp and no conversation going on is held about nine times in ten. "Hey Lamp, …" is answered.

**On lamp-4ace** (the first builder, 04:50; voice `9371018e`, this change on lamp-4ace's base with #891, `LAMP_SPOKEN_TO=on`, `LAMP_ATTENTION=busy-near`):

title: lampOS: the startup hold's replay to Gemini fits its input queue and its audio age bound
body:
Closes #892.

**Kind:** second route only. Nothing changes unless `LAMP_VOICE_SECOND_CONFIG` is set: without it `Rig::second` is `None`, the flush and hold code are not reached, and Gemini's worker is not given `--wait-for-room`. With it set, that flag changes how Gemini's worker meets a full input queue for all its input, not only a replay (change 3).

**Changes:**
1. `d48bed9ec`: a held line given to Gemini at its first Ready is sent 2 commands per tick (`LIVE_REPLAY_PER_TICK`). Before, it went at 8, which overran the link's input queue of 32 (`INPUT_QUEUE_CAPACITY`). The link then dropped the connection as `Backpressure`, reported as `local`. That is what happened in PR #885 run 2, 37 ms after Ready. The second route's replay stays at 8 per tick.
2. `5aa07ac48`: `STARTUP_HOLD_US` is derived from Gemini's audio age bound: `MAX_INPUT_AGE` minus the 300 ms lead-in minus a 300 ms margin, which is 1.9 s (it was 3 s). The line goes to live only while the hold is running. Without this, a line held past about 2.2 s would replay a block that Gemini's worker refuses as stale, and the worker would end.

3. `5ab0fbd6d`, `ac0b66abd`, `5ea41b401` (the reviewer's P2s and P3): with `--wait-for-room`, given by the coordinator only when a second route is configured, Gemini's provider worker offers a command only when the link's queue has room (`InputSender::has_room`). A command that finds it full waits first in line for up to `ROOM_WAIT_US` (250 ms, past the 200 ms write bound) and then goes as before. A cancellation's End waits the same way, ahead of the next request; the retirement itself stays immediate. Without the flag a full queue ends the connection as it always has.

The cause analysis is on #892. `docs/second-voice.md` is updated (At startup, Pace).

**Tests** (each fails without its fix):
- `coordinator::second::tests::a_line_held_two_seconds_goes_to_gemini_within_its_input_queue`
- `a_line_given_to_gemini_at_the_end_of_the_hold_is_never_too_old`
- `a_ready_after_the_hold_leaves_the_line_to_the_second_route`

- `provider_worker::tests::a_short_stall_under_fast_input_waits_for_room_and_loses_nothing`
- `provider_worker::tests::a_cancellation_in_a_short_stall_waits_for_room_and_keeps_the_link`
- `provider_worker::tests::without_the_flag_a_full_queue_still_ends_the_connection_as_before` (off unless set)
- `coordinator::tests::second_route::the_live_worker_waits_for_room_only_with_a_second_route`

Two existing state-machine tests were adjusted for the new pace. `second_route::...startup_hold_is_over` now compares against the constant.

**Gate** (from `lampOS/`):
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p lamp-voice --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p lamp-voice --lib second`: 111 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- `coordinator::tests::second_route` (serial): 8/8 in 2 of the last 3 runs. Two timed cases (#739 family) each failed once and passed on rerun.

Kind: test fixture preparation, enabled only by `#[cfg(test)]` and explicit scenario scopes. Production defaults remain unchanged.

Kind: off unless set. Only with `LAMP_OTHER_LANGUAGE=sorry` in the voice's unit (the provider worker's `--ask-unclear`), and only with the attention rule (`LAMP_SPOKEN_TO=on`). Without it no flag is passed, `Attention::ask_unclear` is false, no `ProviderOutput::Unclear` is ever sent, and `ask_again` stays `None`: the worker and loop are as before (the worker test's control: the Hindi transcript without the switch is answered).

In a conversation (`Thread::going_on`, the lamp spoke within 45 s), when a turn's answer begins (`attention::first_output_busy`, beside the sound rule, so cut-ins are covered), what was heard is judged by `not_speech::unclear_in_conversation`: mostly letters of another script than Latin ("हिंदू के स्थान"), or a number alone when the lamp's last line was not a question ("23"; `Thread::lamp_asked`), or, as the first builder added (#926, 06:10), a cut-in over the lamp's answer heard as up to four words, or one word said over and over, none of which is a common English word (`ENGLISH_WORDS`, a small list, not a language detector: "vestido", "miel miel", "Tá.", "Los Ángeles", "mueve mueve mueve"; "Stop.", "Wait.", "Okay.", "No.", "Wait, wait, wait." pass). The coordinator marks such a turn's end `ProviderInput::End { cut_in: true }` when it took over from the lamp's answer (`took_over_turn`); the field is skipped when false, so other ends are as before. Such a turn's answer is held and dropped as a sound's is; the worker sends `ProviderOutput::Unclear { request, why }` before its `TurnComplete`; once the turn is over and the lamp at rest the coordinator commits a written turn of its own with `speak_up::ASK_AGAIN_NOTE` ("Say only, in the language of the conversation: Sorry?"). The trace says why an asking was dropped (`ask_again_dropped`) and what held a due one back (`ask_again_waiting`, `held_by`). title: lampOS: install sets Harness to start at boot as lampos (#811)
body:
Part of #811

**Kind:** the install command only; nothing on a lamp running today changes (no lamp is installed with `lamp-update install`). With Harness present it changes what `install` does by default.

**What:** the first builder's 01:56 recipe on #811. Once Harness is at `/usr/local/bin/harness`, `install` makes `/var/lib/lampos-tasks` `lampos`'s own (0700), runs `loginctl enable-linger lampos`, then `harness service install` as `lampos` with `HOME=/var/lib/lampos-tasks` and its `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. No hand-written unit. Without Harness it says so and goes on.

**When it is skipped:** only if an earlier install recorded it done, in `/var/lib/lampos-update/harness-at-boot`. That record is written only after `harness service install` returned success. The linger file and `harnessd.service` alone do **not** skip it: the CLI writes its unit before registering it and keeps it when a later step fails. So a lamp set up by hand, or left by a failed run, is asked again on its first install. A failure records nothing; the install stops with the reason, for the Harness team.

**Test:** `harness_is_set_to_start_at_boot_once_when_it_is_there`. Absent: said, nothing asked. Present: asked once, not again on a second run. With the unit and linger files left by a failed run: asked again, and recorded only after success. Refused: the install fails with the reason. The post-write case fails without the fix.

title: lampOS: with LAMP_FIRST_WORDS=kept a yield's request begins at the first words said under the lamp's voice (#828 step 2)
body:
Part of #828: step 2's first half, **a yield's request keeps the first words said under the lamp's voice**. It's the first builder's suggestion (#828, 02:05) and is more urgent after their 05:43 cut-ins: late tails were sent and answered wrongly ("Four." to "count to three", an answer in Hindi). It closes nothing. The other half, a stop word heard while the reply is paused, needs words during the pause and comes separately.

**Kind: off unless set.** `LAMP_FIRST_WORDS=kept` in the voice's environment, read by the coordinator. There's no worker flag, and nothing changes without `--turn-taking duplex`.

**What it does.** The duplex rule yields only once a run of blocks is plainly someone over the lamp. What was said before that, under the lamp's voice, was dropped with the 300 ms before the onset (`PRE_ROLL_BLOCKS`). With the switch:
- **Kept audio:** while the lamp speaks, the detector keeps 1.6 s of blocks (`REACH_BACK_BLOCKS`), each with its own detector score before any mask (`TurnDetector::push_heard`).
- **Where a yield's request begins:** 200 ms (`REACH_LEAD_BLOCKS`) before the earliest block of those 1.6 s the detector scores 0.35 or more (`TurnDetector::begin`).
  - It never reaches past a block heard without echo evidence, wherever that block is, because every block of a candidate is checked against what was heard before it is let through.
  - It never begins later than without the switch.
- **The hold:** its decision deadline is still counted from the trigger, and its retained age from the usual pre-roll (`Hold::keeping_first_words`). Without that, a first block 1.6 s back would have cut the deadline to nothing.
- **Bounds:** the mask remembers 320 blocks of hearing instead of 128, and the provider queue's bound grows by the lead.
- **Records:** `duplex_policy` has `first_words_kept_blocks` (160), and each `input_candidate`'s `first_read_at_us` shows where its audio began.

**Measured** on the first builder's two recordings of 01:51, replayed with `lamp-audio replay-aec` and scored with `crates/voice/examples/hearing_replay.rs` ([the evidence](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/tree/fourth/yield-start/lampOS/docs/verification/first-words-20261016)). The table is ms after the played line began; positive means its opening words were never sent:

| Line, over the story | Run | Today | Kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Hey Lamp, … sleepy dragon …" | -6 dB | 1,347 | 57 |
| "Hey Lamp, … pirate …" | -6 dB | 1,303 | 243 |
| "Hey Lamp, … owl …" | -6 dB | 366 | −924 |
| "Hey Lamp, … lighthouse keeper …" | -6 dB | 1,720 | 430 |
| "Hey Lamp, … sleepy dragon …" | now | 2,464 | 1,744 |
| "Wait." | now | 1,175 | −116 |

- Four late starts begin within 0.43 s of the line, and a fifth gains 0.7 s.
- **The cost:** up to 1.6 s of the lamp's own suppressed voice at the front of a request. The owl, which wasn't late, would begin 0.9 s early.
- Candidates made with the lamp quiet are unchanged.
- One late start, 1,337 ms in the "now" run, made no yield, so this doesn't reach it.

**Tests** (each shows nothing changes without the switch):
- `crates/voice/tests/first_words.rs`:
  - a yield's start reaches back to 20 blocks before the first words;
  - it doesn't reach back when not a yield, not kept, or with nothing speech-like;
  - a block without evidence is a barrier, also inside the usual 300 ms;
  - nothing is reached beyond 1.6 s.
- `admission::…::a_lead_of_first_words_is_held_without_shortening_the_decision`: 160 blocks taken with the deadline from the trigger. 161 are refused, and a lead without the switch is refused.
- `coordinator::tests::duplex::with_first_words_kept_a_yields_request_begins_at_the_words_said_under_the_lamp`: through the production hearing, yield, decision and commit. The request begins at block 81 for first words at block 101; without the switch, 30 blocks before the onset. Every block is checked before commit, and the provider queue holds the whole request.
- All the existing duplex tests pass unchanged; the harness takes the same path with the switch off.

title: lampOS: lamp-policy --rules, progress news obeys a person's kept rules about speaking first (#813)
body:
For #813, the Policy's reader of a person's kept rules about speaking first, agreed with the seventh at 02:41. The seventh's #904 is merged: `memory/rules` carries `quiet`, `quiet_mornings`, and per kind `hello` and `news` (`never`, `not_before_minute`, `not_from_minute`, `not_while_talking`). The seventh's #813 waits on this side (#705, 07:05).

**Scope: progress news, the question that may speak first already on `lamp-voice`.** The hello on arrival (#883) obeys `hello` the same way once it merges. `crates/policy/src/rules.rs` already has `Kind::Hello` for it, and the hello's part is built and gated locally on `second/policy-rules` on top of #883.

**Kind:** off unless `lamp-policy --progress --rules`. Without `--rules` the topic isn't listened to, and the report and decisions are as they were (tests).

**What it does** (`docs/policy.md`, "A person's rules about speaking first"):
- The newest `Rules` on `memory/rules` is kept: it is a kept topic, said at each session open and after each rule kept or forgotten. It stays when the voice goes.
- The progress question obeys it as one more hard rule, after `talking` and `told_recently`:
  - `quiet` holds always;
  - `quiet_mornings` holds before noon at the lamp (`--utc-offset-minutes`), and all day if the local time isn't known;
  - `news.never` holds always;
  - `news.not_before_minute` and `news.not_from_minute` hold outside those minutes of the day, and all day without the local time;
  - `news.not_while_talking` holds while `room/state` isn't known to be quiet, as the room is when the answer comes back (the reviewer's 08:06). The question already waits while anyone talks to the lamp; this adds talk that isn't to it, a call or a visitor.
  - A `hello` limit holds no news.
- While a rule holds, no model is asked, and the change is asked about once the rule no longer holds. An answer that comes back after a rule was kept is turned to `wait`, with `guard` `kept_rule`.
- The diagnostics add `progress_held_rule`; the start line adds `rules=true`.
- The newest `Rules` is obeyed whoever it names. The Policy doesn't know who is at the lamp now, so a rule errs toward quiet.

**Tests**, none needing a lamp:
- `crates/policy/src/rules.rs`: quiet and quiet mornings by the hour, with the time known and not; each typed limit for its own kind only (never; 08:59, 09:00, 21:59, 22:00 and 00:00 against not before 09:00 and not from 22:00; not while talking in a quiet, busy and unknown room).
- `crates/policy/src/progress.rs`, `a_kept_rule_holds_progress_news_and_no_model_is_asked`: `wait` with no model asked, counted once per change; quiet mornings until noon; a rule forgotten holds nothing; `news.not_while_talking` held in a busy or unknown room and not in a quiet one; a `hello` limit holding no news; an answer after a rule was kept turned to `wait`.
- `progress.rs`, `a_yes_that_comes_back_into_a_room_now_busy_is_held_by_not_while_talking`: asked in a quiet room, the yes taken up in a busy or unknown room is a `wait` (`kept_rule`), in a quiet one `say_now`, and the record keeps the room it was asked in.
- `crates/policy/tests/progress.rs`, through the Policy's real loop on a bus:
  - `with_rules_a_kept_rule_holds_progress_news_and_no_model_is_asked`: the typed `news.never` published on `memory/rules` holds a change, no model is asked, and `progress_held_rule` is 1. Forgotten, the change is asked about and a yes is said.
  - Without `--rules`, nothing of the Policy's subscribes to `memory/rules` and the report has no `progress_held_rule`.
- `main.rs`: `--rules` parsed, refused without `--progress` or given twice.

**Gate** on the M2 Max, on `b5185b121` (on `lamp-voice` `e5aa43747`): fmt and clippy `-D warnings` (24 crates) pass; `lamp-policy` 168 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored; the workspace build passes.

**On lamp-4ace** (the first builder, with the seventh):
1. Add `--rules` to `lamp-policy --progress …`; the start line should say `rules=true`.
2. With a task running, say to the lamp "Don't bring me news of my work before ten." The seventh's `keep_rule` should keep it typed as `news.not_before_minute 600`; `lamp-bus tap memory/rules` shows whether it did. Before 10:00 local, `progress_held_rule` in `lamp-bus tap diagnostics` goes up and no progress note is said; at or after 10:00 the next change is asked about.
3. "Forget that rule": the next change is asked about at once.

**Most likely wrong:** the room. `not_while_talking` relies on `room/state`, which the voice publishes; if the room is often `unknown` on the lamp, that rule holds news all the time.

body:
Part of #828: a probe for step 2's second half, a stop word heard while the reply is paused. That half needs words during the pause, from the speech-to-text the second voice already uses, through the company relay on lamp-4ace. The first builder asked for its speed to be measured first (#828, 03:15): the time from the first held block to the first word back, which a 1.1 s pause has to wait for. It closes nothing.

**Kind: a probe, run by hand.** `lamp-voice stt-check CONFIG WAV [ROUNDS] [--held-ms MS]` is a new subcommand. Nothing the lamp runs calls it. The one change to running code is that the second voice's `SttStream` now records when the first words came back (`first_words()`). The words, the timing and the journal are as before.

**What it does:**
- It streams a recorded line (16 kHz mono 16-bit) to the speech-to-text that `CONFIG` sets up. `CONFIG` is the file `LAMP_VOICE_SECOND_CONFIG` names.
- The first `MS` of the line go at once, as a paused reply's held audio would, and the rest at the pace it was said.
- It prints one line a round: `connect_ms`, `first_words_ms` (from the first audio sent to the first result with words, interim or final), `audio_ms`, `final_after_audio_ms` and the final `words`.
- Three rounds and nothing held, unless said; at most 20 rounds and 1,600 ms held. It reads the credential file the config names, so on a lamp it runs as root.

**For example:** a line made on the Mac as the scenes make theirs, then copied to lamp-4ace (a recorded stop word from your bundles works too):
```sh
# on the Mac
say -o stop.wav --file-format=WAVE --data-format=LEI16@16000 "Stop."
# on lamp-4ace
sudo lamp-voice stt-check /etc/lampOS/voice/second.json /tmp/stop.wav 5 --held-ms 600
```

- `second_provider::net::stt::tests::the_first_words_are_timed_from_the_first_result_with_words`: a result with no words is not words; the first interim with words is timed within 50 ms of when it came; the time stays readable after the finish.
