title: lampOS: lamp-skills, the physical skill format, and Welcome back as its first skill (#938)
body:
Fixes part of #938

**Kind:** off unless the service is installed. `lamp-skills` is a new part with its own unit template, `deploy/units/lamp-skills.service`. No lamp's folder and no product unit carries it, and nothing enables it. Nothing in the voice changes: `speak_up.rs` Arrival is untouched. The Policy's ask has its own switch inside the program. Without `LAMP_SKILLS_ASK=skip`, every run is answered no and no call is made. Two tests show this: `without_the_skip_nothing_the_skill_starts_is_done`, and `the_program_does_nothing_without_the_skip`, which checks that no gaze datagram and no actions call are made.

## What is done
- **The format, written in `docs/skills.md`** ("The schema, as `lamp-skills` reads it"). A skill is a folder holding `SKILL.md` (Agent Skills front matter, `name` = folder, `description`), `skill.toml`, `lights/NAME.toml` and `tests/CASE/` (recordings plus `expect.toml`).
  - `skill.toml` has `needs`; a trigger as `[trigger]` or `[[trigger]]`, with `topic`, `when` (`present` or `appears`), `field` with `equals`, `above` or `below`, and `for`, `gap`, `absent_for`, `rearm` and `cooldown`; conditions as `[[while]]`; `[ask] policy`; and `[[do]]` with `body.look_at`, `body.gesture`, `light` (by name or as a table: `colour`/`level`/`for`, or `dim`/`until`) and `say`.
  - An unknown key refuses the skill, and a folder whose name begins with a dot is skipped. Each choice the design does not make is marked *(chosen)* in the doc.
  - Most of Ten's proposed fields (#947) are taken, and the reply on #938 says which were taken, changed or refused. Stuffy air from #947 loads unchanged. Stretch break needs `field = "state"` in its `[[while]]`.
- **`crates/skills`, the `lamp-skills` binary.** It loads `/var/lib/lampOS/skills` and reloads within 2 s when a file changes, keeping cooldowns across the reload. It subscribes once to each trigger topic. It applies `appears`, `absent_for`, `for` and `cooldown` in code, using its own monotonic clock. It publishes `skills/events` at four stages: triggered, asked, answered (with `allowed`) and done (with how each step went).
- **The steps.** `look_at = "face"` sends the largest face as one datagram to `gaze.sock`, in the eyes' own format. `gesture` sends `{"gesture":NAME}` to `mood.sock`. `light` makes one `light_colour` call to the actions part's `call.sock`, with a 2 s timeout.
- **`skills/events`** (`lamp_msgs::SkillEvent`, an event). It is registered in `declaration_of()` and documented in `docs/msgs.md` and `docs/bus.md`.
- **Tests from bus recordings.** `lamp-skills test DIR` loads a skill and runs its cases. `cargo test -p lamp-skills` loads every folder in `lampOS/skills/` and runs its recorded cases, so CI checks every skill. `expect.toml` lists every call a case may make, in order (`at`, `within`, `call`, `args`), or says `none = true`. A case with no recording yet is counted and not run. Welcome back's two cases are real `lamp-bus record` output of `lamp-bus pub --at-us`: `back-after-ten-minutes` (it greets, a short absence does not count, the cooldown holds, it greets again after 40 min) and `there-at-start-then-away`. A test also shows that a case fails when the skill changes: with no cooldown, or with a red light.
- **Welcome back** is in `lampOS/skills/welcome-back/`, and its `skill.toml` is the doc's example word for word.

## What is stubbed
- **The Policy's ask** (#939): the program does not ask anyone yet. `LAMP_SKILLS_ASK=skip` answers yes without asking, and the unit template sets it.
- **`say`** (#939): no say service exists yet. `done` says "a stub, nothing spoken".

## Gaps
- **The look is one sight.** The body takes sights only while the lamp listens or speaks, and needs three in a row, so this datagram alone does not turn the head. A move played on request needs Third's move files.
- **The light stays as set.** `light_colour` is a person's call and has no lease. `level`, `for` and `until = "ends"` are accepted, but are not carried out yet, and `done` says so. Giving the light back needs Third's arbitration.
- **Arrival is not matched.** Arrival's other rules (a face nearer than 0.14 of the picture, there for 3 s, nothing said for 30 s) are not in the doc's example, so they are not in the skill.
- **Not read or run yet:** `moves/`, `sounds/`, `body.move`, `when = leaves/changes` and `tools` (all refused), and `run.py` (refuses the skill). The runtime adds no pause or speaking condition of its own, because the Policy is the one gate (#939).
- **`needs` is not checked.**
- **New dependency:** `toml` 1.1.8 (`parse`, `serde` and `std`; it adds `serde_spanned` and `toml_writer` to the lockfile).
- **CI does not run Clippy** in the ARM64 workflow. I ran it locally (below).

Nothing ran on a lamp. The device run is First's, on lamp-4ace on 17 Oct.

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run --locked -p lamp-skills -p lamp-msgs`: 103 passed. Of these, lamp-skills has 9, including 2 that run the program on a real bus and 2 on Stretch break's and Stuffy air's rules, and lamp-msgs has 3 new ones.
